description: HTTP header names and prefixes with Ferrum Edge semantics: gateway assertions, diagnostic response headers, internal markers, mesh control headers, and admin API headers, including standard HTTP ETag and If-Match. Names and prefixes match case-insensitively. Availability records the first Edge tag containing the surface. From Edge v0.9.15 the gateway writes its request assertions after it has resolved a client's Connection nominations at HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 ingress; the src/proxy/headers.rs provenance note gives the rule.

provenance.note: Connection nominations (ferrum-edge#6090, issue #6087, from v0.9.15): HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 ingress removes every field a client's Connection header nominates before any plugin runs, and rewrites Connection to keep only the close option and the request hop-by-hop names connection, keep-alive, proxy-authorization, proxy-connection, te, trailer, transfer-encoding and upgrade. Host, Content-Length, Expect, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Port, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Real-IP and the configured FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER are protected and keep their client values for routing, framing and trusted-proxy client-IP resolution. A nominated Authorization is removed before authentication. Gateway assertions (consumer identity, X-Authenticated-Identity, claim_headers destinations, X-Geo-Country, path-param captures) and transformer-added headers are written afterwards, so a client nomination cannot remove them. HTTP/2 rejects Connection and is unchanged. Gateway-owned assertion names match ASCII case-insensitively with _ equivalent to - (field_names_equivalent_for_backends), the folding CGI-style backends apply.

not_headers.note: OpenAPI document extension fields read by the API-spec import (docs/api_specs.md), not HTTP headers.

headers.name: x-consumer-
headers.edge_behavior: Gateway-owned consumer assertion namespace. Matching is ASCII case-insensitive and treats _ as equivalent to -. The gateway may emit only its authenticated identity values beneath this prefix; backend boundaries reject client or plugin values across the whole prefix, and it is forbidden in request and response trailers. From v0.9.15 the same gateway-owned check (is_consumer_assertion_header) also covers the exact name X-Authenticated-Identity, listed separately.

headers.name: X-Consumer-Username
headers.edge_behavior: Set by the gateway only after a principal is resolved; never trusted from clients. Any client copy is removed before dispatch. From v0.9.15 (ferrum-edge#6088, issue #6082) the value is only the username of a gateway Consumer that the authentication flow mapped. An external identity or display claim without a mapped Consumer is sent as X-Authenticated-Identity instead, and external authentication no longer maps a principal to a Consumer by matching a username, ID or custom ID. Up to v0.9.14 this header fell back to the external display identity, then the raw external identity.

headers.name: X-Consumer-Custom-Id
headers.edge_behavior: Set by the gateway only after a principal with a custom_id is resolved; never trusted from clients. Any client copy is removed before dispatch. The principal is a mapped gateway Consumer; from v0.9.15 an external identity no longer maps to a Consumer by matching its custom ID.

headers.name: X-Authenticated-Identity
headers.edge_behavior: Gateway-owned external identity header (ferrum-edge#6088, issue #6082). Set only when a request authenticated without a mapped gateway Consumer: the provider's display claim when one is configured and present, otherwise the external authenticated identity. For jwks_auth and oauth2_introspection the display claim is the provider consumer_header_claim, then the global consumer_header_claim, then the provider's effective consumer_identity_claim. An external display value, not a gateway-verified Consumer assertion; backends must not treat it as proof of a mapped Consumer. Never sent with X-Consumer-Username, and not sent when a plugin suppresses consumer identity headers. Matching is ASCII case-insensitive with _ equivalent to -: client copies are removed before any plugin runs and plugin copies are scrubbed before dispatch, on every protocol path, and the name is forbidden in request trailers. Refused as a configured header destination at config load (request_transformer, claim_headers, Gateway API RequestHeaderModifier and similar header mutation rules).

headers.name: X-Geo-Country
headers.edge_behavior: Set by the gateway only after a successful GeoIP lookup. Any client copy is removed before dispatch. From v0.9.15 (ferrum-edge#6090) matching treats _ as equivalent to -, so a client X_Geo_Country is removed too.

headers.name: x-ferrum-
headers.edge_behavior: Ferrum-owned header namespace. Forbidden in request trailers sent to a backend and in gRPC end-of-stream trailers. Individual members below have narrower rules.

headers.name: x-path-param-
headers.edge_behavior: Ferrum-owned path-parameter namespace. Forbidden in request trailers sent to a backend. From v0.9.15 (ferrum-edge#6090) matching is ASCII case-insensitive with _ equivalent to -, so a client X_Path_Param_Id is removed beside the gateway's route path-param capture.

headers.name: X-Gateway-Error
headers.edge_behavior: Gateway-owned diagnostic response header. Every dispatch path strips a backend copy, in headers or trailers, before the gateway writes its own value. Values are the closed vocabulary in vocabularies/gateway-errors.json. Not authenticated.

headers.name: X-Gateway-Upstream-Status
headers.edge_behavior: Gateway-owned diagnostic response header, present only when the load balancer routed through its all-unhealthy fallback. A backend copy is stripped. Not authenticated.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Original-Content-Encoding
headers.edge_behavior: Internal compression-plugin marker for the pre-compression encoding. Never forwarded to a backend.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Grpc-Web-Trailer-Names
headers.edge_behavior: Internal grpc_web response-header bridge for trailer-name provenance. Consumed and removed before the client-visible response; a backend copy is stripped.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Grpc-Web-Shadowed-Trailers
headers.edge_behavior: Internal grpc_web response-header bridge for shadowed trailer values. Consumed and removed before the client-visible response; a backend copy is stripped.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Grpc-Web-Accept-Rejected
headers.edge_behavior: Internal grpc_web response-header bridge for the plugin's own Accept-negotiation 406. Consumed and removed before the client-visible response; a backend copy is stripped.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Mesh-Protocol
headers.edge_behavior: Optional HBONE CONNECT marker between Ferrum mesh peers (value hbone, or a datagram-over-HBONE value).

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Mesh-Tunnel-Reuse
headers.edge_behavior: Stamped by a destination on the HBONE CONNECT 200 only while the admission fence holds that tunnel.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Namespace
headers.edge_behavior: Selects the namespace of an admin API request; absent means the default namespace ferrum. A routing selector, not an authorization boundary.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Provisioned-By
headers.edge_behavior: Optional provisioning-client identifier. Fills an absent labels.provisioned-by on created resources. Must occur once, be nonblank, contain no control characters, and be at most 512 bytes; the value is trimmed. Grants no authority.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Config-Cursor
headers.edge_behavior: Covering live-apply cursor of a database-mode config mutation, as {topology_epoch}:{sequence} (issue #4139).

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Namespace-Unserved
headers.edge_behavior: Present with value true when an accepted mutation targeted a namespace this process's data plane does not route (issue #5447).

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Notification-Severity
headers.edge_behavior: Header on email notifications sent by the gateway.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Notification-Event-Action
headers.edge_behavior: Header on email notifications sent by the gateway.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Diagnostic-Ref
headers.edge_behavior: Opaque gateway-minted diagnostic reference (fd1_<32 hex> or fd2_<8 hex>_<32 hex>), off by default (FERRUM_DIAGNOSTIC_REFS). Gateway-owned whatever the setting: backend and hook copies are stripped. Resolves via GET /diagnostics/v1/refs/{ref}; body is schemas/diagnostic-ref/v1.

headers.name: X-Ferrum-Diagnostic-Owner-Replica
headers.edge_behavior: On a diagnostic-reference lookup 404 from a replica that did not mint an fd2_ reference, names the owning replica id, only for a caller that passed the scope and namespace checks.

headers.name: ETag
headers.edge_behavior: Standard HTTP header. Row CRUD reads emit an opaque quoted strong tag bound to kind, namespace, id and complete stored state, including credentials redacted from ordinary consumer reads. The v0.9.11 admin-only verification read and conditional backup row maps share those tags. Conditional backup also emits a distinct coherent namespace tag equal to conditional.namespace_etag. No tag on cached row fallback or write responses; credential-complete verification and conditional backup never use cached fallback and require audit admission before response with Cache-Control: no-store. Shared admin JWT secrets allow replica agreement; secret rotation invalidates tags. Released v0.9.12 GET /deployment-snapshot emits a separate original quoted deployment-v1 token equal to namespace_etag, with admin-only unfiltered secret-complete evidence, mandatory security audit admission and no-store. Backup namespace and row tags cannot authorize this deployment profile. From v0.9.13 the conditional backup namespace tag and the deployment-v1 token MAC a bounded SHA-256 of the canonical snapshot (namespace_snapshot.v2 and deployment_snapshot.v2 domains) in which stored spec and other binary content counts as SHA-256 and length; tags issued by v0.9.12 or earlier keep their syntax but no longer match. A namespace over the 64 MiB canonical bound gets 507 and no tag. Edge v0.9.14 documents the conditional backup ETag as a namespace state token equal to conditional.namespace_etag, not a validator of the response bytes: two exports of unchanged state share it although their bodies differ (exported_at). Use it only as If-Match on POST /restore?confirm=true for that namespace, never for caching or If-None-Match.

headers.name: If-Match
headers.edge_behavior: Standard HTTP precondition header. Row PUT/DELETE for proxies, consumers, upstreams and plugin configs compare complete stored row state under the namespace admission lease; weak tags never match, strong lists match any member, and * checks existence. The v0.9.11 POST /restore?confirm=true exception requires the coherent namespace tag from conditional backup on the same namespace: atomic comparison and complete replacement, including empty replacement and lease entry/commit fences. Row tags and body metadata do not authorize restore; namespace wildcard/malformed/empty headers return 400, stale or weak-only tags 412, unsupported topology 501, unavailable state/lease 503. Omission preserves unconditional restore. Released v0.9.12 DELETE /proxies/{id}?conditional=true&cleanup_orphaned_upstream=false and PUT /api-specs/{id}?conditional=true instead require exactly one ORIGINAL strong quoted deployment-v1 token from GET /deployment-snapshot. Missing/weak/wildcard/list/duplicate/wrong-profile authority or ambiguous modes are 400; stale dependencies are 412. Comparison and selected writes share entry/commit transaction fences; no fresh-token retry, whole-namespace restore or unconditional fallback. apply=async is refused. Other mutating routes refuse If-Match with 400. Automatic recovery cleanup requires the explicit deployment acknowledgement, never transport status alone. From v0.9.13 namespace and deployment tags issued by v0.9.12 or earlier fail closed with 412 and change nothing; a namespace over the 64 MiB canonical bound gets 507 (deployment mutations report durable not_started before the transaction and not_committed inside it). Do not retry a 507 for unchanged state. Edge v0.9.14 documents that a deployment-v1 token fences the whole namespace, so any other consumer, credential, trust, registry-metadata or resource write in the namespace makes it stale (412). A 503 store failure before the mutation transaction reports durable not_started, one inside the rolled-back transaction not_committed, and only a failed commit or commit acknowledgement unknown.
